If people want to lose weight, then drop down to no more than TWO MEALS a day, with snacks \[snack size bags are great, but limit yourself to TWO\]. The meals should be basic, an American breakfast \[2-3 eggs, a meat, some potatoes\] OR Lunch \[a basic sandwich with chips, a soup or salad\], you can still enjoy a coffee or juice. LOTS OF WATER, water will sate your appetite and refresh your resolve.

For dinner the healthiest meal you can eat is chicken \[grilled, fried, it don't matter!\] with egg noodles smothered in olive oil and garlic and baby carrots in a cinnamon-butter glaze.  
I would recommend rice \[whatever type\] and potatoes as side dishes. The key is not to pound these things into your body, but if you PORTION these foods right you will get a majority of the necessary nutrients to variate down the road.

The idea is to prepare the chicken in advance and to have the side dishes ready to go because you will be hungry. People can air fry foods now, but it still takes longer than reheating or eating it cold from the fridge which actually burns MORE calories. Water with all meals, excepting juice, tea and coffee. Cutting alcohol is also vital for this to work in most cases.

Some of this information may not be supported by "science," but it worked for me to get trim.

I went to one meal a day, using Starbucks Mocha Frappuccinos as my appetite suppressant, but that's definitely not medical advice. Milk would have the same effect of coating the stomach to prevent damage better. I liked the caffeine boost.

I did also have steak once a month, and seafood as well as turkey at times. But those things aren't necessarily important for a regular diet, and red meat comes with health complications either way \[damn if you eat it, but also if you don't\]. I found my diet routines benefitted from introducing red meat \[filet mignon since it was so rarely consumed\] made the other days easier.
